text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the hedging is appropriate: 13.1% vs 3.3% expected, 30% of 99215s on 0-1 condition patients, 29 charts, 2 below billed, 4 documented 99215s with 0 below billed. The 'inconclusive' leaning fits the tool output. But the summary is weakly usable. Next steps start with two below-billed claims (a 99213 and a 99214) while asking for 99215 charts, so the targets do not fit the request. The cited low-complexity examples are the least suspicious ones (single diabetes patients), not the strongest ones such as the 0-condition Z09 visits. Key context is omitted, such as the 3.97 ratio and the higher 99215 share at every complexity level. It also leaves out that all four documented 99215s supported high MDM, and that the one documented-high example C0039596 is on the low-complexity list. Some of the note-signal and audit-trail text is noise.","problems":["Next step asks for a targeted sample of 99215 charts but lists C0039482 (99213) and C0039558 (99214) as the starting charts, which are not 99215s","Example 99215 claims chosen are the mildest low-complexity cases (type 2 diabetes, 1 condition) rather than 0-condition claims like C0039553 or C0039622 (Z09)","Does not tell the investigator that the 4 documented 99215s all supported high MDM, which weakens the concern, and does not name them","Omits the 99215 share by complexity tier and the 3.97 ratio, which would show the excess is spread across all tiers","The 'late 0%, unsigned 0%' note-sign line, 'No audit trail was received', and the MISSING_SIGNATURE deficiency in the exchange are presented without interpretation","Missing items are only partly flagged; the summary says too few documented 99215s but gives no concrete request scope or size"]}
